A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CR-CTC research work. All 19 pages, including Figures 1–2, Tables 1–17, equations, references, and Appendices A.1–A.7, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original speech-recognition experiments on LibriSpeech, Aishell-1, and GigaSpeech, component ablations in Section 4.3, and additional decoding, hyperparameter, and Conformer results in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, and appendix results, including the Conformer comparison in Table 17.

M1.justification: The two-view CR-CTC procedure, consistency objective, stop-gradient operation, and increased time masking are unchanged. The SR-CTC procedure in Appendix A.1 is also identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LibriSpeech, Aishell-1, and GigaSpeech datasets for English and Mandarin speech recognition. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every corresponding experiment, including CTC, CTC/AED, pruned transducer, EMA-distilled CTC, SR-CTC, and the auxiliary-head comparisons. Appendix Table 17 retains the same Conformer comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and the appendices retain identical preprocessing, augmentation, model configurations, training budgets, evaluation metrics, and decoding procedures. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The self-distillation, masked-prediction, peak-suppression, and auxiliary-head analyses in Section 4.3 are unchanged. The appendix decoding comparisons, hyperparameter sweeps, and Conformer evaluation are also retained without modification.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates and token-level averages. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains CR-CTC Zipformer-L WERs of 2.02%/4.35%, and Appendix Table 17 retains Conformer CR-CTC WERs of 2.43%/5.78% on test-clean/test-other.

T1.justification: The CTC definitions and loss formulations in Equations 1–8, including the appendix SR-CTC and EMA-distillation objectives, are identical. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about improving CTC, matching transducer and CTC/AED performance, and explaining CR-CTC through self-distillation, masked prediction, and peak suppression.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and interpretations of generalization and ablation results are unchanged. Correcting a spelling error in the peak-suppression discussion does not alter its meaning, and no limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: Implementation details, augmentation parameters, hardware and epoch tables, model configurations, and the icefall code-access information are unchanged. Embedded hyperlink targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and the positioning relative to prior consistency-regularization, self-distillation, and CTC work are identical. The updated publication-status header does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 corrects 'generalization abality' to 'generalization ability' in Section 3.3. It also replaces 'Preprint. Under review.' with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp; the remaining prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–17 retain identical content, formatting, captions, and placement. Page layout is unchanged; the header wording update is a text edit covered under P1.

improvement.justification: v4 makes one spelling correction and updates publication/version information. The scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility details, and visual presentation remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, so these cosmetic edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
